first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and memory_31 and memory_86 both show that simplification drives measurable adoption lift. Verifying memory_31 (signup simplification for SMB activation) and memory_73 (promotional pricing effectiveness) will clarify whether to lead with friction reduction or pricing response. However, simplify_onboarding is the stronger play here: it directly addresses the measurable completion decline, targets the broad base (self-serve SMB), and has dual supporting evidence (memory_31 on signup fields, memory_86 on onboarding duration). Activation is also down 6% QoQ—memory_91 shows messaging helped, but onboarding friction is a more direct lever on both metrics. Promotional pricing addresses the competitive threat but risks margin and doesn't solve the activation/completion decline. A standard-experiment rollout on simplified onboarding can run this week, measure the QoQ slope, and preserve optionality for pricing response if needed next week.

mid.rationale: Archive verification confirms simplify_onboarding is the right choice this cycle. Memory_31 (signup simplification) delivered +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue with only -1% retention risk—a sustainable profile. Memory_73 (promotional pricing) shows why NOT to chase the competitor: +31% signup but -12% 30-day retention and failed renewal cohorts. Pricing wars erode long-term value. Current situation: activation down 6% QoQ, onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Simplifying onboarding directly targets both metrics and aligns with primary objective (maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue). Memory_86 adds confidence that duration reduction works broadly. Memory_91 suggests activation messaging can compound gains. Standard experiment scale allows controlled measurement this week with clear success criteria (completion rate recovery, activation lift) and minimal downside. If successful, can layer activation messaging next cycle.

final2.rationale: Competitive pricing pressure is real, but memory_73 archive data is definitive: targeted promotional pricing destroys cohort quality and renewal rates. Churn conversations doubled, but the right response is not a pricing match—that accelerates a race to the bottom and undermines long-term revenue. Hold course on simplify_onboarding. It addresses root metrics (activation -6%, completion -4%) and provides genuine competitive differentiation through product experience, not price matching. Faster onboarding and better activation reduce churn drivers that have nothing to do with price. For price-sensitive accounts actively churning this week, the sales org can execute hold conversations emphasizing upcoming feature value and improved time-to-value. Simplify_onboarding experiment already launched creates momentum to communicate: we're investing in making your experience better, not discounting. This preserves margins, protects future cohort quality, and directly addresses the operational declines. Leadership pressure to react to pricing is understood, but reactive discounting violates our primary objective. Recommended: stay in experiment; brief sales on value narrative; monitor cohort quality metrics closely.
